text:
Marathon Petroleum has climbed nearly 21% over two weeks, with today's modest gain capping a strong rally driven by escalating Middle East tensions and their impact on oil prices. Iran's intensified attacks on shipping and Saudi Aramco facilities—including a container ship sinking in the Strait of Hormuz—have pushed crude oil prices sharply higher (US oil at $96.24/barrel, world crude at $125.44), which improves refiner margins by raising the value of refined products relative to input costs. Refineries are running at 92.7% capacity, and diesel inventories remain tight, putting pressure on supply and supporting prices for the fuel that refiners like Marathon produce.

The broader rally reflects how geopolitical disruption to Middle East supply translates directly into profitability for U.S. refiners—higher oil prices typically widen their earnings, especially when demand for diesel and gasoline stays strong, which the IEA expects to persist well into 2027 despite supply constraints.
